title: How Long Would You Last Lost at Sea on a Raft? #shorts
situation: ADRIFT ON A RAFT, NO WATER
description_hook: You're adrift on a small raft in a tropical sea, with no shade and not one drop of fresh water. The clock starts now.

beats.say: How long would you last lost at sea on a raft? Tropical water, about 30°C. No shade. No fresh water. Nothing on the horizon.
beats.img: a small orange inflatable life raft alone in the middle of a flat turquoise tropical ocean, harsh midday sun overhead, empty horizon in every direction

beats.say: After 15 minutes, the sun is already damaging your skin. And the water around you bounces it right back up.
beats.img: blinding sunlight glittering off rippling ocean water around the edge of a rubber raft, a bare sunburned forearm resting on the side

beats.say: You need about 1 litre of water a day. Seawater is 3.5 percent salt. Drink it, and you pee out more than you drank.
beats.img: a cupped pair of hands lifting clear seawater over the side of a raft, sparkling droplets falling back into the deep blue ocean

beats.say: Lose 15 to 20 percent of your body water and it kills you. In this heat, that can take as little as 3 days.
beats.img: an empty raft drifting under a blood-red sunset over a glassy calm sea, long shadows on the water, no land anywhere

gumi.say: Gumi's odds: five percent. Water everywhere, and not one drop is yours.
